summary: The 2026 SBIR/STTR reauthorization. Ten sections amending section 9 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 638): research security, Phase II strategic breakthrough funding, proposal limits, Phase III education and improvements, technical and business assistance, data collection, extension to 2031 with FY2026 carryover, and extension of pilots including Direct to Phase II.
why_it_mattered: The 2026 reauthorization ended a six-month lapse in SBIR/STTR authority and rewrote the programs' terms to 2031: Strategic Breakthrough awards, per-firm proposal limits, a security review and Phase III directions. Every SBIR record in this guide reads against it.
key_facts: Public Law 119-83; approved April 13, 2026; 140 Stat. 755; short title "Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act"; enacted as S. 3971.
Sec. 9(a): section 9(m) date changed from "September 30, 2025" to "September 30, 2031"; section 9(n)(1)(A) (STTR) changed from "2025" to "2031".
Sec. 9(b): an agency with funds remaining at the end of fiscal year 2026 from amounts required to be expended under subsection (f)(1) or (n)(1) may carry them into fiscal year 2027 for SBIR/STTR.

Sec. 2: new paragraph in 9(g) (SBIR) and parallel text in 9(o) (STTR) requiring agencies to evaluate whether a small business concern "presents a security risk for any reason" using the subsection (vv) due diligence process, disclosures, and coordination with the intelligence community, Federal law enforcement and counterintelligence.

Sec. 2: adds denial grounds (D), (E), (F) to the pre-existing foreign-risk paragraph: (D) a security risk connecting the concern to an entity or individual on eight named lists; (E) a security risk whose primary source is classified; (F) a security risk the agency determines warrants a denial.

Sec. 2 named lists: UFLPA Entity List (DHS); Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List (Treasury/OFAC); Section 889 prohibition list (FY2019 NDAA); list of Chinese military companies (FY2021 NDAA); Military End User List (Commerce/BIS); Entity List (Commerce/BIS); FCC list of equipment and services; CBP Withhold Release Orders and Findings List.

Sec. 2: new paragraph (17) requires a process to notify a denied applicant of the determination and its basis "as appropriate pursuant to the discretion of the Federal agency and in a manner that does not compromise national security"; a denial does not bar eligibility in a later award cycle.

Sec. 2(a)(3): subsection (vv)(2) due diligence expanded to cover cybersecurity practices, patent analysis, employee analysis, foreign ownership and financial ties, foreign affiliations of covered individuals/owners/key personnel, investment relationships, technology licensing or joint ventures, and business relationships in foreign countries of concern.
Sec. 2(b): a GAO study requirement changed from "3 years" to "8 years".

Sec. 3: "strategic breakthrough allocation" = an amount from the SBIR allocation under (f)(1) of "not more than 0.50 percent" of the extramural R/R&D budget, for agencies whose required SBIR expenditure exceeds "$100,000,000".

Sec. 3: strategic breakthrough award = "not more than $30,000,000" to a small business concern including affiliates, in a single award or series of milestone-based awards; total period of performance "not more than 48 months".

Sec. 3 eligibility: not less than 1 prior Phase II award; not less than 100 percent matching funds from new private capital and/or new funding from a government agency under a program other than SBIR/STTR Phase I or II; demonstrate a technology that is an effective solution, as determined by market research.

Sec. 3 Department of Defense-only conditions: a commitment for inclusion in a program objective memorandum from an official at program acquisition executive rank or higher; meets high priority requirements or operational needs of a military department; not less than 20 percent of the required matching funds from new DoD funding outside SBIR/STTR Phase I/II.
Sec. 3: agency must complete contract awards using the allocation not later than 90 days after receiving a proposal.
Sec. 3: new paragraph (6) of subsection (aa) exempts strategic breakthrough awards from the award-size limit and the SBA waiver requirement in (aa).

Sec. 3(c): each eligible agency must brief Congress within 60 days of enactment on whether it plans to use the authority. Sec. 3(d): the section and its amendments cease to have effect on September 30, 2031.

Sec. 4: new subsection (aaa): each agency's SBIR or STTR program director must set, equally for all small business concerns, a limit on the maximum number of proposals a concern may submit in response to Phase I and Phase II solicitations; the limit may be on a fiscal-year, per-solicitation, or per-topic basis. The statute does not fix a number.

Sec. 4: waivers on a topic-by-topic basis for topics that are time-sensitive and urgent to the mission; approval/disapproval within 15 days; no more than 5 percent of an agency's SBIR and STTR topics in any fiscal year; report to Congress within 30 days of setting or changing limits or granting waivers.
Sec. 4 timing: limits to be established "not later than 90 days before the start of fiscal year 2027 and each fiscal year thereafter".
Sec. 5: SBA to establish Phase III training for contracting officers and the agency acquisition workforce (Phase III awards, agreements, data rights, sole-source contracting).

Sec. 6(a): Procurement Center Representatives directed to advocate for maximum practicable use and transition of SBIR/STTR technology to Phase III; SBA must modify the policy directives within 1 year of enactment.

Sec. 6(b): agencies to develop simplified and standardized procedures and model contracts for Phase I, II and III and standardized solicitation provisions/clauses on information needed for Phase III eligibility.

Sec. 7: technical and business assistance: "not more than $6,500 per project" (Phase I) and "not more than $50,000 per project" (Phase II); recipients select the provider or may use funds to hire/augment staff; adds cybersecurity assistance and screening for foreign involvement; I-Corps participation option.
Sec. 8: SBIR.gov database and FPDS must flag Direct to Phase II, subsequent Phase II, strategic breakthrough, and Phase III prime/subcontract awards.

Sec. 10(a): section 9(cc) (Phase flexibility / Direct to Phase II) changed from "During fiscal years 2012 through 2025" to "Until September 30, 2031"; Department of Energy and NASA added alongside NIH, DoD and Department of Education; "or STTR program" added.

Sec. 10(b)-(k): extends to 2031 the civilian Commercialization Readiness pilot (gg), accelerated awards (hh), Phase 0 pilot (jj), administrative funding (mm), increased minimum performance standards (qq), commercialization assistance pilots (uu), due diligence program (vv), STTR military research institution pilot (yy), budget calculation pilot (zz), and the SOCOM pilot. Sec. 10(l) repeals section 5142 of Pub. L. 112-81 (GAO mandate).
Public Law 119-83; enacted April 13, 2026; 140 Stat. 755; short title "Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act".
Sec. 6(a)(1) amends section 9(j)(4) of the Small Business Act so Procurement Center Representatives must advocate for transition of SBIR/STTR technologies to Phase III.
Sec. 6(a)(2): SBA Administrator must modify the policy directives within one year after enactment (i.e., by April 13, 2027).

Sec. 6(b) adds 638(r)(4)(C) and (D): simplified and standardized procedures and model contracts; standardized solicitation provisions and contract clauses on what a firm must show to establish Phase III eligibility.

Sec. 5 adds 638(r)(5) "Workforce training": SBA, with DoD and GSA, must train contracting officers on SBIR/STTR authorities, Phase III agreements, Phase III data rights, and execution of Phase III sole-source contracts.

key_facts: Sec. 4 proposal limit applies to proposals submitted "in response to Phase I solicitations and Phase II solicitations" and is to be "set equally for all small business concerns".
Sec. 10(a) inserts "the Department of Energy, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, and the Department of Education" into section 9(cc).

Matching funds for strategic breakthrough awards: "not less than 100 percent matching funds" from new private capital, new non-SBIR/STTR government funding, or a combination.
Sec. 9: authorization extended from September 30, 2025 to September 30, 2031.

Sec. 4: starting fiscal year 2027, each agency's SBIR/STTR director must set, equally for all small businesses, a limit on the maximum number of Phase I and Phase II proposals a firm may submit; basis may be fiscal year, solicitation, or topic; limit to be established not later than 90 days before the start of FY2027; waivers topic-by-topic for "time-sensitive and urgent" needs, decided within 15 days, capped at 5 percent of topics per year; methodology reported to Congress within 30 days.

Sec. 2: agencies must evaluate whether a small business "presents a security risk for any reason"; denial grounds include a connection to an entity on eight named lists (UFLPA Entity List; Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List; Section 889 Prohibition List; Chinese Military Companies list; Military End User List; Entity List; FCC List of Equipment and Services; Withhold Release Orders and Findings List) or a risk the agency "determines warrants a denial"; denied firms must be notified and remain eligible in later cycles; due-diligence scope under 638(vv)(2) widened; GAO study period changed from 3 years to 8 years.

Sec. 3: Phase II "strategic breakthrough" awards of not more than $30,000,000 per small business; period of performance not more than 48 months; not less than 100 percent matching funds; award not later than 90 days after receiving a proposal; funded from not more than 0.50 percent of extramural R&D at agencies required to spend more than $100,000,000; ceases to have effect September 30, 2031.

Sec. 7: agencies "shall authorize" awardees to select their own TABA provider; TABA now covers cybersecurity assistance and screening for foreign involvement; not more than $6,500 per Phase I project and not more than $50,000 per Phase II project; funds may be used to hire or train staff and for I-Corps participation.

Sec. 8: SBIR.gov database must classify awards as direct-to-Phase II, subsequent Phase II, strategic breakthrough, Phase III prime contract, or Phase III subcontract; FPDS must capture Phase III designations and whether non-SBIR contracts use SBIR-funded technology.

Sec. 10: pilots extended to September 30, 2031 include Commercialization Readiness Program (638(gg)), Phase 0 pilot (jj), administrative assistance (mm), increased minimum performance standards (qq), commercialization assistance pilots (uu), due diligence program (vv).
The Act mentions "data rights" once, as a training topic; it does not amend the data-rights rules.

summary: The governing SBA Policy Directive and still the version posted on SBIR.gov. It defines the three phases, base award guideline amounts, the 50 percent overage rule and SBA waiver, eligibility and work-share rules, data rights, certifications and benchmarks. It pre-dates the 2026 Act and still carries pre-2026 termination dates.
why_it_mattered: The SBA Policy Directive is the operating rulebook the agencies follow for SBIR and STTR: phases, award guidelines, eligibility, data rights and Phase III. It is still the May 2023 version, which is why the guide marks the 2026 act's changes as pending.
key_facts: Effective May 3, 2023.
Phase I (§4(a)): feasibility-related experimental or theoretical R/R&D; normally not more than 6 months (SBIR) or 1 year (STTR); base guideline $150,000 including modifications.
Phase II (§4(b)): continues the Phase I effort; normally not more than 2 years; base guideline $1,000,000 including modifications.

Phase III (§4(c)): work that derives from, extends, or completes prior SBIR/STTR work, funded by non-SBIR/STTR sources; no limit on number, duration, type or dollar value (§4(c)(5)); size limits do not apply (§4(c)(6)); no further competition required (§4(c)(3)); agencies must make a good-faith effort to award to the original awardee and document the file/notify SBA if not (§4(c)(7)).

§7(i)(1): agencies may exceed the guideline amounts by no more than 50%; §7(i)(2): SBA reviews the amounts annually for inflation and posts adjustments on SBIR.gov; §7(i)(4): waiver to exceed by more than 50%, requested before solicitation release, decided within 10 business days, effective for one fiscal year.
§4(b)(5): one additional, sequential Phase II award to continue the work of an initial Phase II.

§4(b)(1)(ii) Direct to Phase II: NIH, DoD and Department of Education, SBIR only, with a written determination of demonstrated feasibility; text says the pilot terminates September 30, 2022 unless extended (out of date; see pl-119-83 Sec. 10(a)).
§4(b)(1)(i) cross-program (STTR Phase I to SBIR Phase II and vice versa); §4(b)(7) cross-agency Phase II with written determinations.
§6: size/ownership per 13 CFR 121.702; PI primary employment (more than one-half of time) with the SBC, or with the research institution for STTR only, at award and during the project.
STTR: not less than 40 percent of R/R&D by the SBC and not less than 30 percent by the partnering research institution.
SBIR: awardee performs a minimum of two-thirds of the research/analytical effort in Phase I and one-half in Phase II.
R/R&D must be performed in the United States, with written-approval exceptions.
Majority-VC/hedge/PE-owned (SBIR only): NIH, DOE, NSF up to 25% of SBIR funds; other agencies up to 15%.
Registration in SBA's Company Registry at SBIR.gov required; information updated no more than 6 months before proposal submission.

§8(b)(4): SBIR/STTR Protection Period begins at award and ends twenty years (or longer at agency discretion) from award. After expiry: Government purpose rights (DOE: unlimited rights). Data must be marked (§8(b)(5)).

§6(a)(7): awardees failing the Phase II Transition Rate or Commercialization Rate benchmark are not eligible to submit a new Phase I (or Direct to Phase II) proposal for one year; thresholds are posted on SBIR.gov.
The directive text still says the programs are authorized "until September 30, 2022, or as otherwise provided in law".

Phase III: work that "derives from, extends, or completes" prior SBIR/STTR work and is funded by non-SBIR/STTR sources (private capital, or non-SBIR federal funds for products, production, or continued R&D).

Phase I/II competition satisfies statutory competition requirements; the agency need not compete again; a justification need only state that the project is a Phase III award deriving from prior SBIR/STTR funding agreements.
No limit on number, duration, type, or dollar value of Phase III awards; no time limit between Phase I/II and Phase III; size limits for Phase I and II do not apply to Phase III.

Special acquisition requirement: award to the SBIR/STTR developer "to the greatest extent practicable"; agency must negotiate in good faith, do market research on whether the firm is available, capable and willing, and issue a non-competitive contract where practicable.

If the agency intends to go elsewhere it must notify SBA in writing before award; SBA may file notice of intent to appeal within 5 business days and an appeal within 10 business days; the contracting officer must suspend action; the agency decides within 30 business days; SBA reports all such cases to Congress.

Protection period begins at award and ends twenty years (or longer at agency discretion) from the date of award; data must be marked; unmarked delivery may be corrected within 6 months; DOE takes unlimited rights after expiry, other agencies government-purpose use.
SBIR: awardee performs at least two-thirds of Phase I and one-half of Phase II. STTR: small business at least 40 percent, research institution at least 30 percent.
Set-asides: SBIR 3.2% (agencies with extramural R/R&D over $100M); STTR 0.45% (over $1B).
Failing the Phase II transition-rate or commercialization benchmark bars new Phase I proposals for one year.
§ 8(b)(2): data rights apply to all SBIR/STTR awards, including subcontracts or subgrants.
§ 4(c)(5): a subcontract to a federally funded prime contract may be a Phase III award.
§ 6(a)(2) STTR: not less than 40 percent of the work by the small business, not less than 30 percent by the partnering Research Institution.
§ 6(a)(2) SBIR: Phase I minimum two-thirds by the awardee; Phase II minimum one-half.
§ 3(cc) Research Institution: U.S. place of business, and either a non-profit institution or a federally funded R&D center.
§ 8(d)(1): written agreement allocating intellectual property rights before an STTR award.

summary: Three appendices: solicitation instructions including the certification forms, reporting requirements, and the foreign-affiliation disclosure template. This is where the existing "covered foreign" disclosure questions and the lifecycle certification timing are written out.
key_facts: Certifications at award, then: Phase I at the time of final payment or disbursement; Phase II prior to receiving more than 50% of the total award amount and prior to final payment or disbursement.

Funding Agreement Certification at award: ownership and control, no more than 500 employees with affiliates, PI more than 50% time, work-share minimums, U.S. performance, no essentially equivalent work funded elsewhere.
Life Cycle Certification: Phase I at final payment; Phase II before receiving more than 50% of the award and at final payment.
